discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

motivation: Hidetoshi Katori conceived the optical lattice clock, in which thousands of neutral atoms are confined in a light lattice tuned to a 'magic wavelength' that cancels the trap's perturbation of the clock transition. He demonstrated the first such clocks with strontium. Jun Ye developed the concept into the most accurate and stable timekeepers ever built, reaching fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and below. He also resolved the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. These clocks have measured relativistic geodesy over height differences of centimetres and set stringent limits on any drift of fundamental constants. They have searched for ultralight dark matter, and they now drive the redefinition of the SI second. Their work shows that extreme precision is itself a route to discovery. It turns the measurement of time into a probe of gravity, the fundamental constants and physics beyond the Standard Model.
